event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AVB’s 2024 Form 10-K treats COVID-19 primarily as an ongoing, medium-term threat that continues to influence cash-flows, development schedules, operating costs and demand patterns across its multifamily portfolio.  All language appears in the “Risk Factors” section, making it prospective rather than a disclosure of already-booked losses, yet the Company details concrete pathways by which another wave of pandemic conditions—or lingering after-effects—could hurt revenue (e.g., rent-collection restrictions, waived fees, foregone revenue), raise expenses (e.g., quarantine clean-up, supply-chain inflation) and delay value-creation projects (construction and redevelopment).  The wording is specific—naming supply-chain disruptions, labor force illness, remote-work migration and government moratoria—but remains largely unquantified.  Given that the initial WHO declaration occurred nearly four years before the filing date, the Time Decay Principle requires that evidence be scored in the moderate band (4-6).  No mitigating actions (e.g., insurance coverage, contingency planning) are provided in the cited sentences, so scores are driven almost entirely by the severity and specificity of the identified exposures, capped for time decay.

evidence_list.snippet: The national and global impacts of a pandemic, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, may present material uncertainty and risk with respect to our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: Expressly links COVID-19 to 'material uncertainty and risk'.
Covers multiple key financial dimensions (financial condition, results of operations, cash flows).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but explicit acknowledgment of material company-wide risk; medium-term event keeps score at 5.

evidence_list.snippet: State, local, and federal entities may impose restrictions, for varying times and to varying degrees, on our ability to enforce residents’ contractual lease obligations, and this may affect our ability to enforce all our remedies (such as pursuing collections and seeking evictions) for the failure to pay rent.

components.reason: Identifies government restrictions directly tied to pandemic conditions.
Highlights a clear revenue-collection impairment pathway (limits on rent collections and evictions).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct threat to cash inflows and receivables makes this one of the more severe forward-looking exposures.

evidence_list.snippet: Consumers whose income has declined or who are working remotely may decide to live in a location other than our markets.

components.reason: Specifies demand erosion linked to remote work and income decline—both pandemic-driven trends.
Effect is potential rather than confirmed.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Moderate score reflects a plausible but still contingent hit to occupancy.

evidence_list.snippet: Demand from students and demand for corporate apartment homes may be negatively impacted by trends in remote learning and work, and the adoption of new online technologies.

components.reason: Notes specific customer segments (students, corporate) likely to shrink due to pandemic-accelerated behaviors.
Forward-looking and unquantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds granularity on vulnerable sub-markets but remains speculative, keeping score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Various state, local and federal rules may require us, in some jurisdictions or for some properties, to waive late fees and certain other customary fees associated with our apartment rental business.

components.reason: References compulsory fee waivers stemming from pandemic regulation.
Applies only to certain jurisdictions, limiting breadth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct but localized revenue leakage; moderate impact warrants a 4.

evidence_list.snippet: These requirements or practices may result in foregone revenue.

components.reason: Explicitly states financial loss ('foregone revenue').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Plain statement of revenue loss, but lacks magnitude; medium-term cap fixes score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Our properties may incur significant costs or losses related to shelter-in-place or stay-at-home orders, quarantines, infection, clean-up costs or other related factors.

components.reason: Highlights 'significant costs or losses'—strong severity language.
Lists multiple pandemic-specific cost drivers (quarantines, clean-up).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Severe language and multi-pronged expense exposure reach the upper bound for a medium-term event.

evidence_list.snippet: Impacts on the general economy and our industry caused by (i) supply chain constraints and (ii) inflation caused by both supply chain constraints and governmental fiscal and monetary policies.

components.reason: Flags macro-economic shocks (supply chain, inflation) tied to pandemic ripple effects.
Covers both industry-wide and company-specific exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Connects pandemic after-effects to broader economic headwinds; notable but generic.

evidence_list.snippet: Supply chain constraints could cause delays in our construction and redevelopment activity, and inflation could cause our construction and operating costs to increase without a commensurate increase in our rental revenue.

components.reason: Direct operational delays jeopardize project timelines.
Inflation-driven cost escalation without revenue offset underscores margin risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pinpoints timing and cost impacts that threaten future cash generation—top of the moderate band.

evidence_list.snippet: Emergency orders shutting down non-essential businesses, limiting congregations of people, and requiring social distancing may at times disrupt our development and construction activity.

components.reason: Cites direct regulatory disruption to development pipeline.
Specifies operational area affected (development and construction).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Regulatory interruption is concrete but not quantified, leading to a mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: To the extent we experience delays in construction, our construction costs may increase and we may not achieve, on the schedule we originally planned, the cash flows that we expect when we begin leasing a completed property.

components.reason: Links construction delays to higher costs and deferred cash inflows.
Time-shifted impact rather than permanent loss.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear articulation of schedule-driven financial drag; moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also delay the start of construction of additional development communities which, if constructed and leased as originally planned, would have been a source of future additional cash flow.

components.reason: Highlights opportunity cost—lost future cash flow from postponed projects.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focuses on foregone upside rather than direct loss, so maintained at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The same factors as described immediately above may also impact our workforce.

components.reason: Extends pandemic risk to human-capital domain.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Statement is broad and lacks detail; minor aggravating factor only.

evidence_list.snippet: A disruption in the normal operations of our workforce, as well as the possibility of illness among our associates or a substantial portion of our workforce, could also adversely affect our operations.

components.reason: Specifies operational disruption and illness risk affecting labor force.
Potential rather than realized impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Personnel disruption is material but presented generically, consistent with a score of 4.
